sentence: This project supports research on how biological sex differences affect health by giving researchers methods such as biostatistics, epidemiology, and bioinformatics.
This project studies the mechanisms that drive metastasis, including how cancer cells move and invade and how the tumor microenvironment affects them.
This project builds a platform to quickly make small therapeutic proteins that work better and cost less, aimed at rheumatoid arthritis.
This project tries to find out which genes change susceptibility to early gestational ethanol exposure, using zebrafish and mice.
This project studies why meningioma outcomes differ across people and how a protein drives tumor growth so treatments can block it.
This project builds capillaric microfluidics that prepare samples for small mass spectrometry systems and tests them with clinical samples.
This project studies the genes and brain changes behind why Lewy body dementia affects men and women differently.
This project studies how a protein that reads RNA modification controls the development of a type of immune cell and the liver injury it causes.
This project builds and maintains microscopes and laser systems that record and change neuron activity in mice performing tasks in a virtual-reality environment.
This project uses survey and health care claims data to study how treatment and outcomes for alcohol use disorder differ for women of different ages.
This project checks the quality of genomic data from cells with a gene deleted and tests whether it can identify genes a transcription factor controls.
This project studies how Merkel cell polyomavirus turns on its early genes, which drive infection and a skin cancer.
This project searches for targets of nerve damage behind each disability in multiple sclerosis models, comparing females and males during young adulthood and aging.
This project uses genetic and chemogenetic tools to study how kappa-opioid receptor systems affect negative mood, thinking problems and alcohol dependence.
This project creates free learning modules that add genetics and genomics teaching to curricula.
This project studies how HIV changes over time to resist drugs, especially integrase strand transfer inhibitors and capsid inhibitors, and how this affects treatment results.
This project uses protein signatures to predict limb and cardiovascular outcomes in people with peripheral artery disease and their response to rivaroxaban.
This project builds prime editing tools to correct a mutation in limb girdle muscular dystrophy, delivered with lipid nanoparticles to patient muscle grafts in mice.
This project studies how a repeat protein interacts with a chromatin remodeling complex and affects gene expression and survival of neurons made from patient cells.
This project uses secondary ion mass spectrometry to image lipids in injured brain tissue and study how lipid peroxidation drives ferroptosis after traumatic brain injury.
